canonical_policy.name: Remote HTTP transport does not leak into Application
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; do not leak HttpResponseMessage or remote transport concerns into Application.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Application abstraction translation, no blind EnsureSuccess, handler business-decision exclusion, independent inbound/outbound decisions, serializer preference and no Domain remote contracts all explicit; BF0090/0091 preserve ambiguity.

context_quotes:
- Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into the Application-facing abstraction; do not leak `HttpResponseMessage` or other remote-transport concerns into Application.
- Keep cache technology out of Domain, and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.

Application defines the abstraction; Infrastructure implements it with `HttpClient`:

Application does not need to know the external service uses HTTP.

Use `DelegatingHandler` for genuine HTTP pipeline concerns — access-token acquisition, correlation propagation, request signing — never for business decisions:

Translate remote responses into the abstraction Application consumes. Do not call `EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` blindly when specific statuses carry contract meaning:

For richer failure semantics translate into explicit Infrastructure/Application outcomes; do not pass every upstream status through to your own API. The outbound retry behavior and the inbound response your API returns are separate decisions.

Configure stable headers (media types) on the client; apply per-request values such as dynamic tokens per request or through a handler — never mutate shared `DefaultRequestHeaders` concurrently. Prefer `System.Net.Http.Json` / `System.Text.Json`, with explicit options when the remote contract differs; do not reuse Domain entities as remote contracts to avoid mapping.

Making one client style mandatory everywhere; dynamic tokens in shared default headers; mapping every upstream failure to the same status; resilience pipelines added without understanding their behavior.

canonical_policy.name: API versioning does not duplicate inner models by default
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Do not create separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has multiple versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the API boundary when practical.

reviews.boundary_analysis: No per-version inner models and practical Api contract isolation match; no prohibition on models changed for genuine domain differences inferred.

context_quotes:

canonical_policy.name: Physical structure follows actual responsibilities
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Do not create speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees, or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets solely to make the repository look architectural.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Real-content directories, feature-local sharing, role names, flat-first subdivision and actual documentation subfolders are already represented. BF0018/0097 preserve naming scope; no sample-tree-as-checklist mandate.

context_quotes:

Make each supporting type's responsibility clear from its name, its directory, or both. Established suffixes:

- `Service` — use-case orchestration;
- `Dto` — data-transfer model;
- `Request` / `Response` — Application operation contracts (HTTP-specific contracts belong to Api);
- `Result` / `Outcome` — operation results;
- `Validator` — validation;
- `Rules` / `Policy` — decision or workflow rules;
- `Factory`, `Mapper`, `Adapter` — creation, mapping, boundary adaptation.

Prefer `TaskWorkflowRules`, `TaskWorkflowPolicy`, or `TaskWorkflowService` over an ambiguous `TaskWorkflow`. Introduce responsibility subdirectories only when a feature accumulates enough heterogeneous types that a flat directory is hard to navigate; avoid generic `Models`, `Helpers`, `Common`, `Utils` buckets.

`AddInfrastructure` registers `AppDbContext`, repository implementations, `IUnitOfWork`, external adapters, the SQL Server provider, `HttpClient` integrations, and resilience handlers when used. Create capability-specific subdirectories under `Services/` when they improve cohesion.

```text
backend/<Name>.Api/
├── Controllers/
├── Contracts/
│   ├── Requests/
│   └── Responses/
├── Middleware/               # only when custom middleware exists
├── Extensions/               # cohesive composition extensions only
├── Program.cs
├── appsettings.json
└── appsettings.Development.json
```

Use `Contracts/` only when transport-specific contracts provide a concrete boundary benefit. Do not move arbitrary code out of `Program.cs` only to make it shorter.

canonical_policy.name: Use structured error contracts
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; keep machine-readable contracts stable and safe.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Structured stable safe errors, validation type distinction, no inconsistent anonymous errors and machine fields rather than human messages match. Default-versus-exact-middleware BF0023 already retained.

context_quotes:
- Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely to create layer-shaped types. Introduce transport-specific request/response contracts when separation from Application models provides a concrete boundary benefit.
- HTTP failures use a structured problem-details error contract whose machine-readable parts stay stable and safe for clients.

- Use `ProblemDetails` for non-validation HTTP failures and `ValidationProblemDetails` for request validation failures; keep their machine-readable fields stable and safe (default).
- Centralized handling of unexpected exceptions uses `IExceptionHandler` with `AddProblemDetails()` / `UseExceptionHandler()`.

| Scenario | Technique |
|---|---|
| Invalid HTTP input | `[ApiController]` validation problem response |
| Simple query not found | Application returns `null`; Api maps to 404 |
| Several expected business outcomes | typed outcome or an adopted Result |
| Unexpected exception | `IExceptionHandler` + ProblemDetails |
| Recoverable external failure | handle/translate at the Infrastructure boundary |
| Client/request cancellation | `OperationCanceledException` + `RequestAborted` branch in the handler |

Avoid inconsistent anonymous error objects and validation coupled to Minimal API endpoint filters in a Controller-based project.

| Rate limiting rejected the request | `429` + `Retry-After` when known (never for validation failures) |
| Unexpected internal failure | `500` via centralized handling and ProblemDetails |
| Acting as intermediary; upstream returned an invalid/unusable response | `502` (do not convert every dependency failure to 502) |
Machine-readable clients rely on stable error codes or contract fields, never on human-readable exception messages. Error-handling technique: the `aspnet-error-handling` skill.

canonical_policy.name: Use semantic success statuses
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Choose 200/201/202/204 according to actual HTTP semantics; do not return 200 for every outcome, 201 merely for an internal row insert, or 202 for already-completed work.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Success and less-common response meanings, repeated DELETE convention, operation identifier practicality and Retry-After conditions represented. Missing 304 representation atom remains existing CIS-L0-U0008, not new this pass.

context_quotes:
- Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics: do not return 200 for every outcome, 201 merely because a row was inserted internally, or 202 for work that already completed.
- A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404 (default).

Generate separate or clearly grouped Swagger documents per supported version when clients need them (`swagger` skill); the documented version must match routing and controller metadata. Versions never override normal HTTP semantics (`http-api` skill).

Policy owners: entry-point responsibilities, success/empty-collection/401/403/409/412 semantics, versioning, documentation truth → `.claude/rules/1-architecture/entry-points.md`; ProblemDetails types and Controllers → `2-technology/aspnet-core.md`; failure exposure → `0-core/security-principles.md`. This skill adds technique and the less-common cases. Keep status-code behavior consistent across similar endpoints.

- `PUT` may return 201 when it creates a resource at a previously non-existing URI.
- 202 fits long-running operations, background jobs, asynchronous imports, queued processing; return an operation identifier or a `Location` when practical.
- 204 fits a successful `DELETE` or an update whose representation adds no value. For repeated `DELETE` of an absent resource choose one convention — 204 (desired state holds) or 404 (resource absent) — and use it consistently across equivalent resources.
- For an empty collection (`entry-points.md`), `200` with `[]` also beats `204`: it preserves the resource representation for clients.

## Less-common statuses

| Situation | Response |
|---|---|
| Conditional request; client's cached representation still valid (`If-None-Match`/ETag, `If-Modified-Since`) | `304` (no representation; not a business "nothing changed") |
| Malformed JSON, invalid shape, binding failure, missing transport-level input | `400` (not for authentication failure) |
| Cannot produce a representation acceptable to the client's content negotiation | `406` |
| Request body media type not supported (e.g. XML to a JSON-only endpoint) | `415` |
| Structurally valid request with invalid semantics (e.g. `startDate > endDate`) | `422` — or `400` when the project deliberately uses 400 for both; follow the established convention |
| Contract requires a precondition (e.g. `If-Match`) but it is absent | `428` |
| Rate limiting rejected the request | `429` + `Retry-After` when known (never for validation failures) |
| Unexpected internal failure | `500` via centralized handling and ProblemDetails |
| Acting as intermediary; upstream returned an invalid/unusable response | `502` (do not convert every dependency failure to 502) |
| Temporarily unable to serve (maintenance, required dependency down, chosen overload semantics) | `503` + `Retry-After` when meaningful |
| Acting as intermediary; upstream did not respond in time | `504` |

For richer failure semantics translate into explicit Infrastructure/Application outcomes; do not pass every upstream status through to your own API. The outbound retry behavior and the inbound response your API returns are separate decisions.

Making one client style mandatory everywhere; dynamic tokens in shared default headers; mapping every upstream failure to the same status; resilience pipelines added without understanding their behavior.
ASP.NET Core rate limiting protects this API from excessive incoming traffic and is separate from outbound resilience; rejected requests get `429` with `Retry-After` when known (`http-api` skill).

When determining real responses consider the whole pipeline — model binding, validation, authentication/authorization, rate limiting, centralized exception handling, other middleware — not only explicit branches in the action. Document `201 Created` (with `CreatedAtAction`/`CreatedAtRoute` when a canonical URL exists) only when that is the runtime contract; never `204` for an endpoint that returns a body. Describe ProblemDetails/ValidationProblemDetails contracts where useful; examples and descriptions never show exception types, stack traces, SQL, connection strings, or paths.
